correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the exact Hong--Kim lift bounds, converts them into a conditional block-entropy estimate, and uses the ergodic theorem to show that terminal zero runs are sublinear whenever the marker has positive invariant frequency. The strict parameter inequality then excludes every marker-positive ergodic measure from maximal entropy. Ergodic decomposition handles arbitrary MMEs, the all-zero fiber identifies the marker-free subsystem with Y, and the source's variable-specification theorem supplies uniqueness and full support on Y. No finite computation is used as proof.

value.rationale: The claim gives a structural measure-theoretic classification of the entire arbitrary-positive-entropy counterexample family: uniqueness of the MME survives one-sided balance even though entropy minimality and full support fail. The strict marker-frequency entropy penalty explains this separation and is not a routine restatement of the equal-entropy inclusion Y⊂X.
